findings.evidence: The distance helpers use `memLp_blockAverage`, `dist_toLp_sq_eq_integral_sq`, and `Contractable.integral_sq_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint`; the latter is declared with `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` at `BlockAverages.lean:193`, and no probability-specific lemma occurs in either proof.
findings.fix: Generalize both helpers to `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`; likewise weaken their private prerequisites `dist_blockAverage_toLp_le_of_disjoint` (line 65) and `dist_blockAverages_toLp_le_via_disjoint` (line 117).
findings.issue: `cauchySeq_blockAverage_prefix_toLp` and `tendsto_dist_blockAverage_window_prefix_toLp` (line 210) assume `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`, although every measure-dependent result used requires only `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`.

summary: The extracted Cauchy and window helpers retain an unnecessarily strong probability-measure assumption; their proof chain only requires finite measure.
